findings.defective_text: A setumah opens this unit at oshb:Jer.26.10

findings.defective_text: P06-007: 'The controlled unit_type vocabulary carries no wisdom category'; P06-011: 'The closed vocabulary carries no separate indictment category'; P08-001: 'The unit is typed woe_oracle for its opening formula per the operative-category law' and 'a per-bytes deviation disclosed here rather than in the unit_type field'; P11-008: 'lament_confession is applied here as a per-bytes deviation from the vocabulary's own enumerated roster'
findings.byte_evidence: No text layer supports these: they name the annotation schema (the field name unit_type, the controlled / closed vocabulary, the vocabulary's enumerated roster) and a rule ('the operative-category law') inside row prose, which the register purge bars. check_register.py returns GREEN over these 48 rows (flag_count 0), so no Tier-0 gate sees them -- its CLASSES regexes carry no arm for schema-field or controlled-vocabulary wording. Two of them also surface as universals WARN flags in this scope ('carries no wisdom category', 'carries no separate indictment category'), dispositioned genuine below.
findings.proposed_cure: Restate each as a claim about the text alone (e.g. 'this cursed-and-blessed, heart-searching material reads closest to a judgment oracle'), deleting every reference to the field, the vocabulary and the naming rule.

findings.defective_text: P10-001: 'the campaign holds that crux open rather than correcting it'; P13-003: 'the campaign ties a koh-amar-driven cut to a change of whose mouth carries the formula' and 'a peer reading could reasonably prefer a fresh row at verse 17'; P13-008: 'a peer reading could reasonably prefer splitting the relay from the reading'
findings.byte_evidence: Governance-process and review-actor language in row prose. check_register.py's review_actor arm matches 'peer review', 'peer remedy' and 'reviewer' but not 'a peer reading', and no arm matches 'the campaign', so the suite reports register GREEN (flag_count 0 over these 48 rows) while the purge is breached.
findings.proposed_cure: Replace the process voice with the textual ground -- 'the MT name stands and is not emended here'; 'a koh-amar cut requires a change in whose mouth carries the formula'; 'a fresh row at verse 17 is a defensible rival reading' -- deleting 'the campaign' and 'a peer reading'.

findings.defective_text: P06-011: 'the divine reply now folded into this span (18:13-18:17)'; P10-012: 'this span's own new closing verse, oshb:Jer.29.19'; P10-013: 'A setumah now sits inside this span' and 'the adopted seam this row now opens on'; P13-008: 'the fourth-year notice carrying no month token that opened the row before'
findings.byte_evidence: 'now folded', 'now sits', 'now opens on' and 'new closing verse' narrate a change made to the span rather than describing the text, and 'the row before' is a positional row reference. check_register.py's positional_row_reference arm covers 'that row' and 'the previous/next/preceding/following/prior row' but not 'the row before', and its erratum_repair_narration arm requires an order/remedy/wave/defect token nearby, so all four pass GREEN.
findings.proposed_cure: Delete the change-narrating adverbs and the positional reference: 'the divine reply at 18:13-18:17', 'this span's closing verse', 'A setumah sits inside this span', 'the fourth-year notice at Jer.36.1, which carries no month token'.

findings.defective_text: P06-009 splices יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ from oshb:Jer.17.13 in both strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes; P11-008 splices שׁ֚וּבִי from oshb:Jer.31.21 in device_notes -- neither row mentions ketiv or qere anywhere

findings.defective_text: observed_substrate_signals keys: P09-003 'divine_title.yhwh_tsevaot_elohei_yisrael_stack'; P12-002 'divine_title.full_title_stack'; P12-005, P13-001 and P13-003 'speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh_elohei_yisrael'
findings.byte_evidence: The settled split form is divine_title.yhwh_tsevaot_elohei_yisrael + speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh, and this corpus already carries the settled title key in 15 rows and the settled speech key in 38. P09-003 and P12-002 carry renamed byforms of the title key; P12-005, P13-001 and P13-003 carry a blended key that pulls a divine title into the speech_formula namespace. The bytes separate the two objects at these sites too: the full stack stands in 32 verses (Jer.25.27 inside P09-003's span; Jer.32.14 and Jer.32.15 inside P12-002's), whereas the formulas the three blended rows actually splice carry NO tsevaot -- וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte tier) and כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.34.2, byte tier) -- so the blended key also mis-files them under the full-stack object.
findings.proposed_cure: Rewrite the five entries to the settled split -- divine_title.yhwh_tsevaot_elohei_yisrael + speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh for P09-003 and P12-002, and speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh with a tsevaot-free divine_title key for P12-005, P13-001 and P13-003.

findings.defective_text: 17 seg-layer citations carrying a quote-collation tier label, e.g. P13-001 'A setumah stands one verse before this row's own start, at (oshb:Jer.33.26, byte)'; P13-010 'a paseq also falls at (oshb:Jer.36.23, byte)'; P13-011 'Setumah marks fall at (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte), (oshb:Jer.36.31, byte)'
findings.byte_evidence: 'byte' is collate.py's Hebrew quote-collation tier (byte / nfd / accent_stripped / skeleton / none) and asserts that a quoted run matches the source bytes; these citations quote nothing. The parashah and paseq layers are explicitly not verse bytes -- pmarks_Jer.json paseq_note: seg layer, NOT quotable verse bytes, citable from this inventory only -- so a byte label on them claims a tier the seg layer cannot carry. 17 occurrences across these 6 rows; the same rows label their real Hebrew splices correctly and no other row in this scope does it. check_marks.py is GREEN over these 48 rows (flag_count 0): it validates the seg TYPE and the MT key, not the tier word.
findings.proposed_cure: Drop the tier word from every seg-layer citation, leaving the plain MT key plus the single-witness disclosure already present.

findings.defective_text: A petuchah sits at the seam where this span opens, oshb:Jer.31.6, recurs inside the span at oshb:Jer.31.9 as a setumah

The seam partner P11-007 uses the same sentence frame where the type really is constant (marks['Jer.31.14'], marks['Jer.31.15'] and marks['Jer.31.17'] are all SAMEKH), which is where that template belongs.

findings.defective_text: P11-002: 'A second-person plural imperative pair opens the interior comparison, שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א (oshb:Jer.30.6, byte)'; P12-007: the rationale splice at oshb:Jer.33.10 stops at אַתֶּ֣ם while its gloss reads 'about which you say'
findings.byte_evidence: Gloss extent exceeds splice extent at both sites. Jer.30.6 opens שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ (byte tier): the imperative pair is the first and third words, and the splice covers only the first imperative plus the entreaty particle. findings.proposed_cure: Re-cut each splice to the extent its gloss claims: carry the second imperative into the Jer.30.6 splice and the third word into the Jer.33.10 splice.
